summary_en: Empty it and flatten it, then drop it in the blue bin.
prep_en: Check the bag :: Keep it only if it is clean, dry and intact.|Give it another use :: Use it for dry storage or your next shopping trip.|Recycle when worn out :: Empty and flatten it, then use the blue bin.
note_en: Greasy or food-soaked paper goes in the black bin.
reuse_en: Reuse it first. If it is still clean and sturdy, keep it for another trip. Recycle it when it is no longer usable.
fact_en: Reusing extends the life of paper fibers. Clean, dry paper can then be recycled; grease-soaked paper cannot.

summary_en: Flatten it and keep it dry. Place it in the blue bin.
prep_en: Empty it :: Remove any contents, plastic wrap or foam.|Flatten it :: Open the flaps and fold it flat.|Keep it dry :: Put it in the blue bin away from wet waste.
note_en: Wet or greasy cardboard (e.g. pizza box bottom) goes in the black bin.
reuse_en: Reuse it for storage or packing.
fact_en: Dry cardboard is easy to recycle into new boxes. Wet or greasy cardboard is not.

summary_en: Keep it dry and uncrumpled. Place it in the blue bin.
prep_en: Use both sides :: Scratch paper still has a blank side for notes.|Keep it dry and flat :: Do not crumple or wet it.|Sort it :: Place it in the blue bin.
note_en: Wet or food-stained paper goes in the black bin.
reuse_en: Use the blank side for notes.
fact_en: Clean, flat paper has long fibers that recycle well.

prep_en: Check what it touched :: Plain tissue can be composted.|Sort it :: Use the green bin, or the black bin if it touched chemicals or blood.
note_en: Tissue used with chemicals or for blood goes in the black bin.
fact_en: Plain tissue is paper fiber and breaks down naturally.

summary_en: Empty it, then place it in the black bin.
reuse_en: Bring a reusable tumbler next time.
reduce_en: Bring your own mug or tumbler
fact_en: Paper cups have a plastic lining, so they can't be recycled with paper.
